Author: Gautam Kumar Choudhary

 In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi

sentences.text:
Coram : Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Gautam Kumar Choudhary .........
 For the Petitioner : M/s Pandey Neeraj Rai,
 A. Kishore & R.R. Sinha, Advocates
For the Ed : M/s A. K. Das, Saurav Kr. Singh,
K. Deo & Preetam Mandal, Advocates

.  Apprehending his arrest, petitioner above-named has moved this Court for grant of anticipatory bail in connection with ECIR /2002/ PAT/2009/AD for the offences under Section 3 &
punishable under Section 4 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (herein-after be referred as PMLA in short).
2.

The case of the prosecution in brief is that Sri Madhu Koda held the office of Minster of Mines and Cooperative from February, 2005 to September, 2006 and of the Chief Minister of Jharkhand from September, 2006 to August, 2008.

F.I.R No.09/2009 was registered by the Police (vigilance) for offence under Section 409, 420, 423, 424, 465, 120-B of the IPC and Sections 7, 10, 11 and 13 of the Prevention of Corruption Act against him.

3. It is alleged that during this period Madhu Koda acquired money through corrupt and illegal means and invested the crime proceeds in collusion with his accomplices in acquisition of properties, to remove the taint of the ill-gotten wealth generated by commission of the scheduled offence.
The Enforcement Directorate registered ECIR /2002/ PAT/2009/AD on 08.10.2009 for the offence of money laundering.

4. The CBI, in its investigation in RC No.5A/2010/ AHD- Ranchi filed two charge-sheets, viz.
Charge-sheet No.6 of 2010 dated 12.11.2010 and Charge-sheet No.1 of 2013 dated 21.05.2013.

5. The Enforcement Directorate in its investigation under the PMLA filed successive prosecution complaints under Section 45 of the PMLA against Madhu Koda, his accomplices and various Ram Swarup Rungta vs Union Of India Through The Directorate ... on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172002624/
1 companies involved in money laundering.

sentences.text:
The investigation revealed that proceeds of crime had been laundered not only through a group of persons but also through several legal entities viz.
companies/firms both inside and outside India.
After investigation prosecution complaint has been submitted by the ED against this petitioner and others.
6. It was found that M/s Shivans Steel Pvt Ltd, M/s Kolhan Trading Pvt Ltd, and other companies along with Vikash Sinha were involved in the process of money-laundering.

Cash was received and delivered to the companies who used to issue cheques in the name of Chandra Bhusan Jha and from his companies cheques were issued to the companies belonging to Vikas Sinha, who on his part invested about 6 crore in the company owned by this petitioner in which the petitioner was Director at the relevant time and was responsible for day to day business/banking transactions of the said company.
However, the share certificate was not issued with respect to the investments made.
7. This petitioner along with others had in this way projected the ill-gotten money of Madhu Koda as untainted.

8. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been implicated in this case on the basis of, a supplementary prosecution Complaint, filed on 17.07.2018 by the Enforcement Directorate against Khalari Cements Limited, apart from other companies.

On this complaint,
cognizance was taken by the learned Special Judge, CBI-cum-Special Judge, PMLA, Ranchi on 17.07.2018 itself.

This was followed by another Supplementary Complaint filed on 03.05.2019, in which the directors of M/s Khalari Cements Limited were made accused, namely, Ram Swarup Rungta (petitioner herein) and Sanjay Rungta.
The learned Special Judge, PMLA took cognizance of the offence on 03.05.2019 for offences under Section 4 of the PMLA.
9. It is submitted that petitioner being a senior citizen of about 85 years old has been suffering from many severe diseases including Prostrate cancer.
The certificate issued by one Dr Saumik Chatterjee dated 9.11.22 has been filed wherein it has been stated that the petitioner was suffering from Adeno Carcinoma of Prostrate.
After investigation chargesheet has been submitted and that is no further requirement of custodial interrogation.
It is submitted that Proviso to Section 45 (1) makes specific provision for bail to those who are seriously ill.
Reliance is placed on (2012)1 SCC 40 for bail at the post-chargesheet stage.
10. Learned counsel Sri A.K Das has vehemently opposed the bail application.

It is submitted that whenever Vikash Sinha required money in his companies, he (Vikash Sinha) delivered cash by himself and his employees namely, Abhimanyu, Balaji Patil and others at Kolkata, or from the office of S. K. Naredi, Jamshedpur.

That, normally after receipt of the cash the same was delivered to other companies who used to give cheques in the name of his (Chandra Bhushan Jha's) companies and from his companies cheques were issued to the companies belonging to Vikash Sinha, or any company or person as directed by Vikash Sinha, under the cover of share capital money or unsecured loan.

The service charges varied from 2 to 4%, which he used to keep 0.25% out of it and balance was passed on to other companies providing cheques to his (Chandra Bhushan Jha)
companies.

Purchase of share was sham and was only ploy to invest the crime proceed will be apparent from the fact that no share certificates were in possession and he was not aware whether Ram Swarup Rungta vs Union Of India Through The Directorate ... on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172002624/
2

sentences.text: any share certificates have been issued at all.

11. Further, petitioner was accused not only in this case but had already been convicted in another case being C.C. No.05 of 2014 and R.C. No.219/2013/ E/ 0002 by the learned Patiala House Court,
New Delhi, which related to coal block .

12. After having considered rival submissions advanced on behalf of both the sides and the materials on record, the complicity of the petitioner appears to be writ large in the process of money laundering.
This is a case where the scheduled offence was allegedly committed by the then Chief Minister who was also holding the post of mining minister.
Huge crime proceed so generated was invested in movable and immovable properties, within the country and also abroad, through web of companies in layered manner to give it the colour of legitimacy.

The petitioner being the Director of one such company by an elaborate process of Placement, Layering and Integration got huge sum invested in his company which was the crime proceed generated by the commission of scheduled offence.
The only point that remains to be considered is whether the petitioner is entitled to anticipatory bail considering his age and ailment with which he is suffering.
It has been pleaded that the he is in his twilight stage of life at an age of about 85 years and is presently battling prostate cancer.
His Jail custody will seriously affect his ongoing treatment.
Prosecution complaint has already been submitted and the accused was not arrested during investigation.
Considering the age and the nature of ailment of the petitioner the anticipatory bail application is allowed.

Hence, in the event of his arrest or surrender within a period of two weeks from the date of this order, the petitioner named above shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh) with two solvent sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Court below, subject to the conditions laid down under Section 438(2) Cr.
P.C.

The petitioner will comply with the condition as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Cr.P.C.
(Gautam Kumar Choudhary, J.) Sandeep/
